chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The slanderer of the foundling is penalized (by the Hadd), and the slanderer of the son of al-mula'ana is penalized (by the Hadd).

key_terms.ابْنِ الْمُلَاعَنَةِ: The son of al-mula'ana (child resulting from the imprecation ceremony)
key_terms.قَاذِفُ: The slanderer (one who accuses of illegitimacy)
key_terms.يُحَدُّ: Is subjected to the fixed legal penalty (Hadd)

ai.seo_question: What is the Hadd punishment for slandering a foundling or the son of mula'ana?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the Hadd penalty for Qadhf (slander) applies specifically to those who accuse a foundling or the child of Mula'ana of illegitimacy, distinguishing these cases from general slander. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the precision required in applying fixed punishments, as the status of the accused (the foundling or the Mula'ana child) determines the validity of the accusation and the subsequent legal consequence. It reflects the broader principle that Qadhf requires specific conditions regarding the victim's lineage status to trigger the full penalty.
